title: The Bay Thirteen Blackout
venue: Bayline Golf Social • Fictional Baton Rouge, Louisiana
description: A medium-difficulty mystery at a fictional Baton Rouge golf venue. A sponsor rep dies during a corporate tournament, and the truth hides inside a launch monitor calibration, a private bar tab, and a suspicious bay transfer.

answerKey.method: Disabled the Bay Thirteen safety lock and used a miscalibrated ball feeder to trigger a violent close-range shot, then blamed a guest swing.
answerKey.motive: To stop sponsor rep Priya from exposing inflated tournament charges and fake equipment rentals.
answerKey.keyEvidence: Safety-lock bypass, calibration file, bar-tab refund code, and Priya’s sponsor audit draft.
answerKey.explanation: Rafe controlled the equipment desk and billing records. His calibration file changed Bay Thirteen before Priya arrived, and his refund code appears on the fake rentals she was about to report.

publicClues.title: Case Opened
publicClues.text: Priya Nair, a sponsor auditor, is found inside Bay Thirteen after the corporate tournament pauses for a lightning delay. The turf smells of wet rubber and machine oil, and the ball feeder is still clicking even though the bay is supposed to be locked out.

publicClues.title: Live Scene Update
publicClues.text: A marshal cuts power to Bay Thirteen, but the feeder clicks one more time after the switch is off. Rafe Danton says, “Old machines do that,” before anyone asks about equipment.

publicClues.title: Live Scene Update
publicClues.text: The sponsor table goes quiet when Priya’s tablet lights up with an unsent audit email. The subject line reads: “Bay charges do not match rentals.”

publicClues.title: Live Scene Update
publicClues.text: A guest points out that the feeder tray is too clean except for one oily thumb smear near the manual release.

publicClues.title: Live Scene Update
publicClues.text: The storm moves over the netting. Thunder covers the sound of the maintenance door chime in the security playback.

publicClues.title: Live Scene Update
publicClues.text: A bartender finds a refunded tab under the sponsor account. Rafe says refunds are normal, but the code belongs to the equipment desk.

phone.title: Maintenance Door Chime
phone.text: The maintenance door beside Bay Thirteen chirped at 8:43 PM. Rafe’s device was the only equipment-staff phone inside the service corridor at that moment.

phone.title: Priya’s Unsent Call
phone.text: Priya tried to call the regional sponsor director at 8:41 PM. The call failed during the storm, but the draft note below it says “Rafe controls the rental codes.”

messages.title: Equipment Desk Warning
messages.text: A text from Rafe to a floor runner reads: “Keep Priya off 13 until I reset it.” The message was sent twelve minutes before the incident.

messages.title: Sponsor Audit Reply
messages.text: Priya wrote, “The same clubs are charged to three parties. I need the raw feeder logs.” The reply was never sent.

maps.title: Bay Transfer Log
maps.text: Priya was moved from Bay Ten to Bay Thirteen by an equipment-desk override. The host stand did not make the transfer.

maps.title: Service Corridor Track
maps.text: Rafe’s staff tracker moved from the equipment desk to the Bay Thirteen maintenance door during the lightning delay.

bank.title: Fake Rental Charges
bank.text: The sponsor account was charged for twelve premium club rentals, but only four sets were checked out. The refund routing code belongs to Rafe’s desk.

bank.title: Split Refund Pattern
bank.text: Three past tournament refunds were split into small credits under different initials. The same pattern appears on Priya’s audit sheet.

photos.title: Feeder Tray Photo
photos.text: The feeder tray inside Bay Thirteen is clean except for an oily thumb smear near the manual release. The safety cover is not seated evenly.

photos.title: Launch Monitor Angle
photos.text: The launch monitor was tilted down by a few degrees. That angle would misread a close-range ball as a normal swing path.

social.title: Corporate Tournament Reel
social.text: A posted reel shows Priya walking toward Bay Thirteen while Rafe stands by the equipment door instead of the desk.

social.title: Deleted Sponsor Comment
social.text: Priya had started commenting “Ask for itemized rental logs” under the tournament post. The comment was deleted from her phone, not the public feed.

contacts.title: Witness Statement: Amara West, floor marshal
contacts.text: Amara says Bay Thirteen was marked locked during the storm delay and should not have accepted balls from the feeder.

contacts.title: Suspect Statement: Rafe Danton, equipment manager
contacts.text: Rafe says he stayed at the equipment desk and never touched Bay Thirteen after the lightning delay began. He claims the feeder malfunction was old hardware.

contacts.title: Witness Statement: Celia Tru, bartender
contacts.text: Celia says Rafe asked for the sponsor tab refund printout before Priya was found, even though the audit had not been announced to staff.

contacts.title: Suspect Statement: Nico LeBlanc, corporate player
contacts.text: Nico admits he complained about Priya’s audit but says he only wanted the tournament comped. He says Rafe promised the rental issue would disappear.

notes.title: Safety Lock Scrape
notes.text: The Bay Thirteen safety lock has a fresh scrape under the latch. The mark is clean and sharp, unlike the older scratches around the frame.

notes.title: Calibration File Name
notes.text: The launch monitor calibration file is saved as “weather-reset,” but the edit time is before the storm warning was issued.

files.title: Raw Feeder Log
files.text: The feeder accepted a manual release command at 8:43 PM, even though the bay was marked locked.

files.title: Sponsor Audit Draft
files.text: Priya’s audit draft names the equipment desk as the source of inflated rental charges and requests a meeting with the sponsor director.

browser.title: Search: Override Bay Safety Lock
browser.text: The equipment desk browser searched how to bypass a bay safety lock without triggering the front-end alert.

browser.title: Search: Hide Refund Routing
browser.text: The same browser searched how to split refunds under multiple initials in a point-of-sale export.

openingNarration: The corporate tournament was supposed to impress sponsors. Instead, Priya Nair died in Bay Thirteen while auditing the venue’s rental charges. The machinery, not the leaderboard, is where the first lie begins.
revealScript: Rafe Danton turned Bay Thirteen into a weapon by bypassing the safety lock and changing the feeder calibration before Priya entered. He needed her audit buried before the sponsor money trail reached him.

seriesArc: A fictional Baton Rouge golf lounge mystery collection inspired by high-energy driving bays, private parties, scoreboards, and late-night competition.
lobbyBackstory: You are checked in at Bayline Golf Social during a corporate tournament where sponsor money, rented clubs, and bay technology are part of the show. When the case opens, do not trust the scoreboard alone. Search the bay, process the equipment, and question anyone who benefited from a bad audit.
rsvpExcerpt: A corporate tournament at a Baton Rouge golf lounge stops for lightning, then turns deadly inside Bay Thirteen. The sponsor audit was almost finished, and someone needed the equipment to tell the wrong story.
